$AAOI signs $2.2B LTA with hyperscaler customer. 

- $1.5 billion of 800G transceivers in 2027
- $0.7 billion in lasers between 2028 and 2029

"Customer forecast indicates demand that could exceed $10 billion over the four-year term".
@aleabitoreddit We have to admit It. Management sucks but $AAOI is very well positioned
@aleabitoreddit Is it bad or good news? I mean they said for $5-6bn or there will be more?

Well yes, for $AAOI it's insanely operationally bullish... In terms of $1.5B in 800G revenue for 2027 alone minimum (not including their other LTAs + orders). 

But management commentary is literally trolling. They said "Will be even five times bigger, or even more than that."

And it turned out to be like 1.5x-2x. 

Standalone it's still transformational but management commentary drives me insane

I wonder if we'll see an AI quantum discovery theme emerge in the future, following biotech discovery. 

$GOOGL Deepmind: "Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents":

1. The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depend as much on better algorithms as on better hardware.

2. LLMs have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops

3. AI lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

$ANT has also been recently working on other applications in this field as well: "Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude"

Just found this paper interesting, there might be some interesting beneficiaries if AI could pull forward quantum commercialization timelines.

Always a fun time for markets: "Trump administration set to unveil new tariffs" 

- Japan, South Korea, and the EU could face incremental increases of 2.5-5% percentage points, with potentially steeper increases for Vietnam to India

- "The Trump administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity", complicating US-China trade truce

- New tariff announcement could come as soon as Tuesday

Wow, memory names like $SNDK just keep on dropping.

At a $89B MC they have: 

> $89B minimum in LTAs with contractual price floors supporting at least 80% gross margins

"The floor pricing for those contracts, we said in aggregate, will deliver at least 80% gross margin for every single year" 

> Not including HBF and uncommited capacity (~50% for 2027, ~33% for 2028)

> Customers placing billions in deposits for 2029-2031 capacity already (Morgan Stanley)

I really disagree with the notion that you need need NAND pricing to keep exponentially increasing Q/Q. 

At long as pricing remains elevated and you have duration visibility, lot of these memory companies look very undervalued.
@aleabitoreddit What this is telling me is no one believes in these LTAs or the sustainability of them

Yeah, I think it's a mix of just indiscriminate de-grossing as well as just not believing in counterparties paying the LTAs. 

Even $SNDK can go out and say:

"We came up with these financial guarantees with third-party financial institutions, which basically will flow those funds to us if they don't execute their part of the agreement"

I guess all it takes is time for people to change their minds.
